data.narrative: Alekhya demonstrated mature architectural planning throughout Module 02, decomposing the vague one-sentence Team Collaboration requirement into a complete 10-task dependency graph. When confronted with the BREAK step's conflicting data model assumption between team creation and membership, she recognized that decomposition is fundamentally about defining interface contracts rather than just slicing work. She implemented Task 2 with full adherence to Task 1 contracts, achieving 9/9 passing automated tests.

dimension_scores.observation: Drafted three fully executable prompt specifications with explicit positive deliverables, contextual file references, and negative constraints (no new external dependencies).
dimension_scores.evidence: Created detailed prompts for Task 1, 2, and 3 in progress/task-tree.md that eliminate ambiguity and pass the two-agent reproducibility test.

dimension_scores.observation: Checked Task 1 output against all 4 acceptance criteria, verifying external black-box behavior with dedicated unit tests.
dimension_scores.evidence: Executed tests/team_model.test.js confirming team ID prefix, timestamp equality, empty name rejection, and missing owner rejection.

dimension_scores.observation: Diagnosed the implicit data model mismatch in Task 2 and resolved it by formally writing the interface contract between Task 1 and Task 2.
dimension_scores.evidence: Implemented src/routes/teams.js and verified 9/9 tests passed in 165ms without regression.

dimension_scores.observation: Selected Top-Down decomposition (Option A) to identify the critical path and ensure cross-cutting RBAC and audit concerns were mapped upfront.
dimension_scores.evidence: Documented 10-task tree with critical path Task 1 -> Task 3 -> Task 4 -> Task 6 -> Task 7 -> Task 8 -> Task 9 -> Task 10.

dimension_scores.observation: Delivered high-quality, production-ready artifacts with zero lint or runtime failures, maintaining strict diff boundaries under 150 lines per task.
dimension_scores.evidence: 9 passing unit and integration tests across tests/team_model.test.js, tests/team_routes.test.js, and tests/starter.test.js.

strengths: Rigorous interface contracting: defines explicit boundary specs (inputs, return schemas, error statuses) before delegating tasks to AI agents.
Atomic decomposition discipline: keeps every task bounded under 150 lines with external black-box acceptance criteria.
Critical path awareness: maps dependencies to expose sequential blockers and parallelizable workstreams.
growth_areas: Ready to tackle Module 03: Context Engineering (the Context Triangle: architectural, local, and constraints).
data.recommendation: Advance to Interlude 01 (Therac-25) and Module 03: Context Engineering.
